definitions.explanation: A lord or ruler in feudal Japan. Also used figuratively to describe someone who acts in an authoritative or pampered manner.

examples.english: The lord set out on a journey with his retainers.

examples.japanese: ⟦{江戸時代|えどじだい}→江戸時代：20431_edojidai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{殿様|とのさま}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧⟦{城|しろ}→城：03255_shiro⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{住|す}んでいた→住む：00673_sumu⟧。
examples.english: Feudal lords in the Edo period lived in large castles.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{殿様|とのさま}⟦{商売|しょうばい}→商売：03239_shoubai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{失敗|しっぱい}→失敗：01636_shippai⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: He failed because of his haughty business approach.
examples.notes: 殿様商売: doing business in a lordly, complacent manner; not making an effort to attract customers

notes:
{殿様|とのさま} was the respectful title for feudal lords (⟦{大名|だいみょう}→大名：10378_daimyou⟧) in Japan. Today it is used in historical contexts and figuratively to describe someone who acts entitled or pampered.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {殿様|とのさま}⟦{商売|しょうばい}→商売：03239_shoubai⟧: lordly/complacent business style (not trying to attract customers)
- {殿様|とのさま}ガエル: Japanese tree frog (literally 'lord frog')
- {殿様|とのさま}⟦{気分|きぶん}→気分：01306_kibun⟧: feeling like a lord (being pampered)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Frequently appears in ⟦{時代劇|じだいげき}→時代劇：12968_jidaigeki⟧ (historical dramas) and children's stories about feudal Japan. The image of {殿様|とのさま} is of someone powerful but sometimes comically detached from everyday life.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{大名|だいみょう}→大名：10378_daimyou⟧: feudal lord (historical/formal term)
- ⟦{武士|ぶし}→武士：03989_bushi⟧: samurai, warrior
- ⟦{家来|けらい}→家来：12397_kerai⟧: retainer, vassal
